'''PR''' is the [[function problem|complexity class]] of all [[primitive recursive function]]s—or, equivalently, the set of all [[formal language]]s that can be decided in [[time complexity|time]] bounded by such a function. This includes [[addition]], [[multiplication]], [[exponentiation]], [[tetration]], etc.

The [[Ackermann function]] is an example of a function that is ''not'' primitive recursive, showing that PR is strictly contained in [[R (complexity)|R]] (Cooper 2004:88).

On the other hand, we can "enumerate" any [[recursively enumerable set]] (see also its complexity class [[RE (complexity)|RE]]) by a primitive-recursive function in the following sense: given an input <math>(M, k)</math>, where <math>M</math> is a [[Turing machine]] and <math>k</math> is an integer, if <math>M</math> halts within <math>k</math> steps then output <math>M</math>; otherwise output nothing.  Then the union of the outputs, over all possible inputs (<math>M</math>,&nbsp;<math>k</math>), is exactly the set of <math>M</math> that halt.

PR strictly contains [[ELEMENTARY]].

PR does not contain "PR-complete" problems (assuming, e.g., [[many-one reduction|reduction]]s that belong to ELEMENTARY).

== Hierarchy ==
The PR class can be divided into an infinite hierarchy of increasingly large complexity levels, according to the [[fast-growing hierarchy]].

The <math>\text{F}_0</math> class is the class of problems that can be solved in <math>n + O(1)</math> time. That is, there exists a Turing machine and a constant <math>C</math>, such that given an input of length <math>n</math>, the machine solves it and halts within <math>n + C</math> steps.

The <math>\text{F}_1</math> class is the class of problems that can be solved in <math>\mathsf{poly}(n)</math> time.

The <math>\text{F}_2</math> class is ELEMENTARY.

The <math>\text{F}_3</math> class is TOWER, which can be equivalently written as the class of problems that can be solved in [[tetration]]-time.

The union <math>\bigcup_{n \in \N} \text{F}_n</math> is PR.

In practice, many problems that are not in PR but just beyond it are <math>\text{F}_\omega</math>-complete (Schmitz 2016).
